historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2023-FY2025 USD revenue CAGR (6,385 -> 6,908 = 4.0%/yr), the only same-currency, post-Terminix window; equals organic ~2.5-3.5% plus ~1pp acquired
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 28.9% vs revenue 13.9% and EPS 7.6%: both the equity and revenue CAGRs are dominated by the October 2022 Terminix acquisition (share-funded, ~$6.7bn) and are not an organic growth signal; the equity CAGR is explicitly rejected as the growth source.
historical_growth.notes: Currency break: FY2019-FY2022 are GBP as filed, FY2023+ are USD. CAGRs above translate the GBP start-year figures to USD at period-average GBPUSD (FY2020 1.284, FY2022 1.237; year-end 1.367 and 1.21 for equity). Revenue FY2022 ($4,594m) -> FY2023 ($6,385m) is the Terminix full-year annualisation plus the currency change, not organic growth. FCF CAGRs use reported FCF less SBC (owner basis excluding the lease/termite/one-off adjustments, which are not available consistently before FY2023); owner 3-yr 11.7% vs reported 11.5% -- SBC has grown roughly in line with cash flow, no divergence. All multi-year CAGRs here are acquisition-distorted; the forward driver anchors to the 4.0% FY2023-25 USD window and H1 FY2026 organic growth of 3.6%.

scenario_narratives.base: Rentokil is a $7bn route-based pest-control and hygiene group whose value hinges on two things: whether North America (62% of revenue) can get back toward market growth after four years of post-Terminix underperformance, and how much of the recurring termite, transformation and acquisition cash the headline 'Free Cash Flow' leaves out actually recurs. The base case takes management at its post-July-2026 word -- NA savings reinvested for volume, no 20% margin, organic growth ~3% against a 6% market -- and charges the termite cash ($120m/yr, tapering) and one-off cash ($115m/yr, falling to a permanent 0.5%) in the flows. Adjusted EBITDA margin improves only 130bp over six years. Growth of 4-4.5% through FY2029 is organic ~3% plus bolt-on M&A that costs ~1.7% of revenue a year, which is charged as capex. Leverage is inside the 2.0-2.5x range and no equity raise is needed.
scenario_narratives.bull: The new team (Duffy, Carrasco, Jochim) does what Ransom's could not: separating Residential and Commercial leadership, the Dallas training hub and Branch 360 lift NA retention above 82% and organic growth to ~5% by FY2028, while International keeps compounding at 4-5% with 19-20% margins. Reinvested savings earn their keep, so group adjusted EBITDA margin reaches 23.5% (still short of Rollins). The termite claims pool behaves as a run-off book -- litigated-claim volumes stop rising, cash falls below $50m/yr by FY2032 -- and transformation spend ends in 2027. The stock re-rates from ~11x to a Rollins-adjacent multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: The margin-target retirement was the first admission of a structural problem, not a one-off reset: NA Residential lead flow keeps weakening, National Accounts churn is not fixed, and Rollins and well-funded PE roll-ups keep the share-loss going. Savings are spent on marketing that does not convert, so margins drift down rather than up. The termite provision keeps being topped up every half ($392m and rising, inflation assumption already lifted to 3.2%), making $120m/yr a permanent cost of the Terminix deal. Leadership churn (five senior changes in six months) produces another guidance miss in February 2027. No growth premium survives: terminal growth 2% and a 15x cap.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A defensive, recurring-revenue consolidator valued on unlevered owner FCF after every recurring cash cost the company's own 'Free Cash Flow' definition adds back or nets away: lease payments (treatment B), termite damage claim cash, transformation/integration cash and bolt-on acquisition spend. On that basis FY2025 owner FCF is ~$516m against a headline $615m, and the current price sits close to the base-case value -- the 40% share-price fall since the July 2026 results has removed the premium, not created a bargain. The value is in the termite and transformation lines tapering as management says they will; the risk is that they do not.
key_risks_to_valuation: North America organic growth: every 1pp of sustained organic growth below the base path is worth roughly 8-10% of equity value; the July 2026 Residential lead-flow warning is the live data point

Termite damage claims: the provision has been topped up every period since the Terminix acquisition; the base case assumes cash tapers from $120m/yr to ~$70m/yr by FY2035, the bear holds it flat -- this is the single largest judgment in the flows
Margin path: the 20%+ NA margin target is retired and no replacement is promised until February 2027; the base case allows only ~130bp of group adjusted EBITDA margin expansion over six years
Recurring 'one-off' cash: $100-135m/yr for three consecutive years; the model treats 0.5% of revenue as permanent, which is more than the company's headline FCF assumes and less than its own history
Leadership and reorganisation risk: new CEO, NA CEO, CMO, Chief Transformation Officer and a two-division restructure all within 2026
Currency: USD flows against a GBp quote; a 5% GBP move shifts the pence value by 5% with no change in the business
Refinancing at higher coupons: 2025 USD bonds at 5.0-5.625% versus legacy paper; cash interest is outside the unlevered flows but inside the WACC

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for RTO.L at inputs.price_as_of (LSE regular close); 52-week range 293.5-507.0p. GBPUSD=X and NYSE ADR RTO from the same endpoint for the fx_note parity check.
data_sources.financials: RTO.L_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, FY2019-FY2025 + H1 FY2025/H1 FY2026); FY2025 Annual Report (adjusted EBITDA, FCF reconciliation, one-off and adjusting items table, lease note B4, termite provision narrative); H1 FY2026 interim report (net debt note 9, adjusting items, FY2026 technical guidance); kpis table (CashTaxesPaid, InterestIncome, LeaseLiabilities, DividendsPaid, AdjustedOperatingProfit).
data_sources.qualitative: RTO.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10): competitive position vs Rollins, termite liability, margin-target retirement, leadership transition, FY2026 guidance items.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report consolidated cash flow statement, 'Share-based payments' $28m (RTO.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:12322); no separate equity-award tax line is disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes kpi = 0), so the combined figure equals the add-back
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows are USD (reporting currency switched from GBP in the FY2025 Annual Report; FY2023-24 comparatives re-presented in USD). Quote is LSE pence. fx_rate = 100 / 1.3233 = 75.569 GBp per USD, i.e. per-share USD value x 75.569 = pence. Rate: Yahoo GBPUSD=X 1.3233 at 2026-10-09T21:29Z. Parity check: NYSE ADR RTO closed $20.24 (1 ADS = 5 ordinary shares) -> $4.048/share / 1.3233 = 305.9p vs LSE close 303.0p, a 1.0% gap attributable to the New York session trading after the London close. Direction and magnitude confirmed.
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted average ordinary shares for diluted EPS, 2,535m (FY2025 AR note, RTO.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:3384; H1 FY2026 interim note carries the same count). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice. buyback_cash = 0 -- Rentokil does not repurchase; shares to satisfy awards are issued to the employee trust (1.5m in FY2025), so the flat count is a modelling convention funded by the SBC charge, not by buybacks.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Company-defined net debt at 30 June 2026 is $3,575m INCLUDING lease liabilities of $543m. Lease treatment (B) puts the lease cash inside the flows, so net_debt here is the ex-lease figure: $3,575m - $543m = $3,032m = borrowings $5,545m (1,944 current + 3,601 non-current) - cash $2,471m - $42m fair value of debt-related derivatives (H1 FY2026 note 9, RTO.L_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:1764-1788). Gross cash of $2.47bn is large because the group pre-funded 2026-27 maturities; it is netted in the bridge, and finance income is outside adjusted EBITDA so there is no interest-income double count (interest_income = 0).
inputs.owner_fcf_walk: FY2025 continuing operations, $m, unlevered: Adjusted EBITDA 1,430 (20.7% of revenue 6,908) - lease payments 223 (192 principal + 31 interest, AR note B4 line 13218) - SBC 28 - legacy termite damage claim cash 95 (inside OCF via movement on provisions; NOT in the one-off cash line, which shows '-' for termite) - cash impact of one-off and adjusting items 100 (NA transformation 76, acquisition/integration 18, other 6; the company ADDS this back to reach its $615m FCF) = owner EBITDA 984 (14.2%) - D&A ex right-of-use 200 (adjusted D&A 360 = 1,430 - AOP 1,070, less ROU depreciation 160) = EBIT 784 - unlevered cash tax ~157 (20%: cash tax paid 100 plus the ~$55m interest shield on $222m cash interest at 25%) = NOPAT 627 + D&A 200 - capex ex-ROU 196 - bolt-on M&A 115 = owner FCF 516 (7.5% of revenue). Reconciliation to the company's $615m: 615 + 222 cash interest - 55 tax shield - 100 one-off cash - 115 M&A - 20 disposal proceeds - 5 associate dividends + 59 working-capital outflow reversed (engine runs WC at zero) = 601; the residual ~85 is the SBC add-back and provision movements outside termite that the company's OCF carries and the component build does not. The France Workwear divestiture ($397m proceeds, Sept 2025) is already in the June 2026 cash balance and the continuing-ops revenue/EBITDA base excludes Workwear, so it is neither double-counted nor omitted.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in USD, the currency of the flows: risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta 0.95 (defensive route-based services, moderate leverage) -> cost of equity 9.0%; pre-tax cost of debt 5.2% (April 2025 USD bonds at 5.0%/5.625% blended with lower-coupon legacy EUR/GBP paper), 25% tax -> 3.9% after tax; weights 77% equity ($10.2bn market cap at 303p x 1.3233) / 23% ex-lease net debt ($3.0bn) -> 7.8%, rounded to 8.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: execution, competitive and termite risk are charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, not again in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. Full lease cash (principal + interest, $223m FY2025 = 3.2% of revenue) is deducted inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities ($543m) are EXCLUDED from net debt; cash-tax EBIT uses D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (2.9% of revenue). Never both.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are $2m (FY2025 balance sheet) -- immaterial, no adjustment.
inputs.termite_treatment: Legacy Terminix termite damage claims are charged IN THE FLOWS, not in the equity bridge. The provision balance ($392m at 30 June 2026) has been topped up every period since acquisition ($201m charge vs $95m cash in FY2025; $44m charge vs $46m cash in H1 FY2026) and management explicitly disclaims any guarantee claims trends improve, so a bridge deduction of the discounted balance would understate it. Instead the annual cash outflow is modelled as a percentage of revenue inside ebitda_margin_path: FY2026 at the guided $115-125m (1.65% of revenue), tapering as the acquired customer pool churns (base to 0.7% by FY2035, bull to 0.4%, bear held at 1.7%). The provision balance is therefore deliberately NOT deducted again in the bridge.
inputs.one_off_treatment: Cash cost of one-off and adjusting items (NA transformation, integration, other) is charged in the flows inside ebitda_margin_path: FY2026 at the guided $110-120m (1.6% of revenue), FY2027 at ~1.2% while the NA transformation completes, then a permanent 0.5% (base) for a company doing 30-40 bolt-on deals a year. The company adds these back to reach its headline FCF; this model does not.
inputs.m_and_a_treatment: Bolt-on acquisition spend (FY2025 $115m, FY2026 guided c.$120m, ~1.7% of revenue) is charged inside capex_pct_path because the revenue growth path includes the ~1-1.5pp/yr of acquired growth it buys. capex_pct = capex ex-ROU (2.8%, guided $190-200m) + M&A (1.5-1.7%), tapering to 4.0% by year 10 as growth decelerates.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, non-US, material leases, USD flows vs GBp quote -> owner-fcf.md plus owner-fcf-adaptations.md parts a, b, f). Fresh build, no prior DCF. ebitda_margin_path in this file is NOT the company's adjusted EBITDA margin: it is adjusted EBITDA margin less the termite cash and one-off cash percentages described above (FY2025 equivalent 17.85% = 20.7 - 1.4 - 1.45). Base year FY2025 continuing operations (France Workwear excluded). Year 1 = FY2026. Horizon 10 years because the owner margin is still recovering from the FY2026-27 transformation/termite trough. Price is the LSE regular close, not after-hours.

bear.rationale: The July 2026 Residential lead-flow weakness persists; NA organic growth stalls at 1-2% as Rollins keeps taking share; reinvested savings buy no volume so adjusted EBITDA margin drifts from 20.7% to 19.5%; termite cash stays at 1.7% of revenue indefinitely (provision keeps being topped up); recurring restructuring never falls below 0.8%. M&A spend is cut with the growth. Terminal growth 2.0%, cap 15x for a business that has lost its growth premium.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 5.5% AER: H1 was +6.7% reported (3.6% organic + M&A + a USD-weakness translation tailwind), H2 slower on the flagged Residential lead-flow weakness and a fading FX tailwind. FY2027-29 4.5% = ~3% organic (below the ~6% US market, continued share loss to Rollins assumed) + ~1.5pp bolt-on M&A at the guided $120m/yr. Decelerating to 3.0% by FY2035.
base.margin_rationale: Underlying adjusted EBITDA margin 20.9% FY2026 (H1 20.8% vs 20.4% pcp) rising only to 22.0% by FY2031 -- the retired 20%+ NA margin target means the $100m NA savings are reinvested, so only ~half flows through; 22% is below Rentokil's own pre-Terminix 23% and Rollins' ~24%. Less termite cash 1.65% -> 0.7% and one-off cash 1.6% -> 0.5% gives the path recorded. Cash tax ramps 20% -> 25% (adjusted ETR guidance 25-26%) as the US intangible deductions roll off.
base.terminal_rationale: 2.5% terminal growth (pest control grows at or above GDP; this is below the ~6% US market and the company's own 4-5% medium-term ambition). Cap 20x house default; Gordon at 8%/2.5% gives 18.6x so Gordon binds.

bull.rationale: Duffy's reinvestment closes the NA organic gap to ~4.5-5% by FY2028 (still below the 6% market); adjusted EBITDA margin reaches 23.5% by FY2031 (Rollins-like NA economics plus International at 20%); termite cash tapers to 0.4% of revenue as the legacy pool churns and litigation normalises; transformation spend ends on schedule in 2027 with one-offs falling to 0.3%. Terminal growth 3.0%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: the July 2026 margin-target retirement and the flagged Residential lead-flow weakness are live, management itself disclaims any improvement in termite claim trends, and five senior leadership changes in six months put execution on an unproven team. Bull cut from 35% to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right at once -- a NA organic recovery, margin expansion despite reinvestment, and termite stabilisation -- none of which has yet shown up in a reported period. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
